insights.summary_short: The Northwind Solar Farm project aims to generate 82 GWh annually with a capacity of 48 MW, backed by a budget of 41.5 million euros. Construction starts in June 2026, with community benefits including discounts and a fund.
insights.summary_detailed: The Northwind Solar Farm project, sponsored by the Halden County Energy Cooperative, is located 12 kilometers north of Marlow. It will have an installed capacity of 48 megawatts using 96,000 bifacial panels on single-axis trackers, generating an expected 82 gigawatt-hours annually. The total capital budget is 41.5 million euros, approved on 4 March 2026, including a 3.2 million euros contingency reserve. Construction is set to begin in June 2026, with grid connection targeted for the second quarter of 2027, and Brightline Builders as the main contractor. Environmental measures include a 15-meter hedgerow buffer and sheep grazing for vegetation management. Additionally, Marlow residents will benefit from a 10 percent discount on electricity tariffs and a community fund of 50,000 euros annually from project revenue.

key_points.text: The Northwind Solar Farm project is sponsored by the Halden County Energy Cooperative.
The solar farm will have an installed capacity of 48 megawatts and will use 96,000 bifacial panels.
Expected annual generation from the solar farm is 82 gigawatt-hours.
The total capital budget for the project is 41.5 million euros, approved on 4 March 2026.
Construction is planned to start in June 2026, with grid connection targeted for the second quarter of 2027.
Brightline Builders is the main construction contractor for the project.
A 15-meter hedgerow buffer will surround the site to protect local wildlife.
Residents of Marlow will receive a 10 percent discount on electricity tariffs due to the project.
A community fund will receive 50,000 euros per year from project revenue.
